content: This medication is not a substitute for the advice of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. How to Use: Before starting fosfomycin, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, if available. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically as a single dose of one packet (sachet). Dissolve the contents of one packet in half a glass (4 ounces or 120 milliliters) of cold water and stir until fully dissolved. Do not use warm or hot water. Your symptoms should improve within 2 to 3 days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include diarrhea, nausea, headache, vaginal discomfort, or dizziness. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking fosfomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. If you develop symptoms of a kidney infection, such as pain in your side or lower back, fever, or chills, contact your doctor immediately. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate dizziness. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This product may contain sugar and/or aspartame. Use caution if you have diabetes, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any other condition requiring you to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. Fosfomycin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Fosfomycin passes into breast milk in small amounts but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not contain all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not individualized medical advice and does not replace the advice of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
